identityReview: Patricia Espinosa Cantellano, Mexican diplomat born 21 October 1958 in Mexico City; distinct from Ecuadorian María Fernanda Espinosa and other namesakes. International relations licenciatura and postgraduate studies in Geneva, without an inferred master’s or PhD. UNFCCC appointment 18 May 2016, arrival 18 July 2016, final service day 16 July 2022. Former Mexican foreign minister, current onepoint5 founding partner and CEO. COP16 and General Assembly Third Committee chairmanships are not the General Assembly presidency. Second German posting has an explicit 2012/2013 source discrepancy.
lifeStatusEvidence: RMI’s 23 September 2026 signed-platform announcement quotes and identifies Espinosa as onepoint5 CEO; IMAGO/ZUMA Press records her 10 November 2026 COP31 speaking appearance. These support recent activity, not completed policy implementation or current UN office. Image pixels were not inspected.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read relevant passages of the 2013 legislative review, UNFCCC historical biography and appointment/renewal/Cancún pages, Graduate Institute alumni profile, Mexican Sustainable Finance Council biography, company leadership, RMI cooperation announcement and IMAGO editorial metadata. Read Commons and original Flickr metadata and licence link; no image pixels.
corrections: Read relevant biographical passages and proposed resolution of the Second Committee report dated 13 August 2013. Birth: 21 October 1958, Mexico City, according to the certified record submitted to the committee; the underlying certificate was not personally inspected. Education: licenciatura in international relations at El Colegio de México and postgraduate international law studies in Geneva, without a specified master’s or doctorate. Career service began 16 September 1981; promotion to ambassadorial rank in January 2000; foreign minister 1 December 2006–30 November 2012. First German posting January 2001–April 2002; Austria/Vienna June 2002–November 2006; economic affairs in Geneva 1982–1988. Nomination received 17 July 2013, hearing/report 13 August. The file-path date 14 August is not a credentials-presentation date. The report submits a proposed ratification resolution; no separate plenary vote was inspected. Its future work programme is not treated as accomplished policy.

Read UNFCCC historical biography: appointment 18 May 2016, arrival 18 July 2016, service through 16 July 2022. Confirms foreign ministry, COP16 presidency, Third Committee chairmanship in 1996 and Austria/Vienna service. It dates the second German posting from 2012, whereas Mexican institutional sources give 2013 and the appointment review took place in 2013. The profile explicitly preserves this discrepancy. Wording connecting a 1996 committee role with the 1995 Beijing Platform is not repeated as reverse-time causation. Postgraduate studies do not establish a specific completed master’s or doctorate.

Read Geneva Graduate Institute alumni profile, class of 1987. It corroborates the institution and career but does not identify a particular postgraduate degree; class year is not assumed to be an award date. The Graduate Institute is not silently replaced with the University of Geneva. Repeated 2012 Germany-start and 1996/Beijing wording does not independently resolve those discrepancies. Description of Paris implementation does not establish sole authorship of the 2015 agreement.

Read Mexican Sustainable Finance Council biography: current onepoint5 founding partner and director; foreign minister 2006–2012, UNFCCC 2016–2022, Germany 2013–2016 and Austria 2002–2006. Ambassador Emerita in 2012 is a career distinction, not a new active posting or UN appointment. The decoration list was not independently checked or expanded into profile achievements. Company role is corroborated by its own current page.

Read onepoint5 leadership and services page identifying Patricia Espinosa Cantellano as CEO and Founding Partner. Its stated work covers strategic advice, geopolitics and sustainability. Other employees’ qualifications and dates were not attributed to her. No company incorporation date or exact personal starting date was established. Similarly named Onepoint, 1point5 and PointFive businesses were excluded. Marketing claims do not independently prove client outcomes.

Read UNFCCC announcement published 19 May 2016 with a New York dateline of 18 May: Ban Ki-moon appointed Espinosa after COP Bureau consultation, to succeed Christiana Figueres. The preceding praise of work on Paris 2015 refers to Figueres. Publication on 19 May, appointment on 18 May and arrival on 18 July are separate dates. Secretary-General, COP president and Executive Secretary are distinct offices.

Read 3 July 2019 announcement of a second three-year term following communication from the UN Secretary-General’s office and consultations with the COP Bureau. That date is the announcement, not an independently verified first day of the new term. Institutional praise is attributed. Reappointment does not imply continued UNFCCC service after July 2022.

Read official introduction to the Cancún Agreements: reached 11 December 2010; mitigation, adaptation, transparency, technology and establishment of the Green Climate Fund. The scheduled 29 November–10 December conference dates are compatible with an overnight conclusion on 11 December. Institutions, targets and pledges do not prove all funding was paid or emissions cuts achieved, and are not solely personal accomplishments. A later review of a 1.5°C goal is not an already achieved Paris commitment in 2010. No full negotiating-record or disbursement audit.

Read RMI announcement dated 23 September 2026 confirming a signed memorandum with onepoint5 and launch of the Global Islands Resilience and Energy Security Investment Platform. It quotes Espinosa and identifies her with Ije Okeke in the caption. The initial Pacific focus, project preparation, financing and wider replication are plans, not completed construction or funding for every project. A separate 22 September event listing was an advance announcement; it was not used to replace the dated signed-memorandum account. This partner release is not an independent impact assessment.

Read IMAGO/ZUMA Press catalogue 0880941476: capture date 10 November 2026, COP31 speaking appearance in Antalya, media dimensions 6000×4000. The site warns captions may be translated or enriched with AI. This is corroborating activity metadata, not a transcript or verification of every policy statement. The photograph is rights managed with a Germany/Austria/Switzerland restriction, and was not purchased, downloaded or used as the open portrait. No image pixels or speech video were inspected.

The second German posting discrepancy remains explicit. Press statements and event metadata support activity rather than every policy claim.

translationReview.scope: All 32 fields in seven foreign languages reviewed for birth and education, service entry and rank promotion, first German and Austrian postings, exact foreign-minister dates, Third Committee versus General Assembly presidency, Cancún agreements, second German term with source discrepancy, UN appointment versus publication versus arrival, 2019 announcement versus term start, 2022 end of service, current consultancy role without an invented start date, and the 2026 signed memorandum versus planned project delivery.
